headline: Protest organizer at Jantar Mantar confused after police demand 'pre-approved list of grievances' in alphabetical order
body:
A local protest coordinator at Jantar Mantar was left scratching his head Tuesday morning after being informed by on-duty officers that his group’s list of demands had been rejected for failing to follow proper 'alphabetical syntax.' The organizer, who had gathered twenty activists to highlight issues regarding water supply, was told that 'A for Abysmal Infrastructure' was acceptable, but 'W for Water' had to be re-filed under 'I for Inadequate Liquid Assets.'

“The sub-inspector was very polite but firm,” said the organizer, who had spent three hours securing a permit just to hold the banner. “He explained that because the Constitution doesn't explicitly mention 'Water' before 'Agriculture,' we were technically violating the rhythmic structure of civil dissent. He suggested I go home, rewrite the petition in iambic pentameter, and return with a permit stamped by someone who can confirm my protest isn't ‘tonally disruptive’ to the nearby traffic flow.”

Officers on the scene further clarified that while the right to assemble is preserved, the right to assemble ‘without causing confusion in the department’s filing system’ is a secondary concern. The protest group has since been seen wandering the site, attempting to rearrange their placards to spell out their grievances in a way that is less offensive to the local stationery supply cabinet.
caption: When you just want to protest but the grammar police take it literally. Who knew civil rights were indexed by font choice and alphabetization? 📝📢 #JantarMantar #ProtestLife #BureaucracyProblems (satire)
